;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[Battle of Farah]]
***[[Taliban]] forces claim to have taken control of the western city of [[Farah, Afghanistan|Farah]] after two days of fighting. It is the second provincial capital to be temporarily taken over, after a [[Battle of Kunduz (2015)|similar assault]] on [[Kunduz]] in 2015. [http://www.post-gazette.com/news/world/2018/05/15/The-Taliban-claim-they-ve-taken-control-of-a-western-Afghanistan-capital-Farah/stories/201805150135 (''Pittsburgh Post-Gazette'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Economy of the United Kingdom]]
**The [[United Kingdom|British]] government renationalises the [[Virgin Trains East Coast]]-operated [[East Coast Main Line]]. The [[Department for Transport]] will run the rail service until 2020. [https://www.reuters.com/article/britain-railway-stagecoach/britain-renationalises-east-coast-rail-line-idUSFWN1SN0N2 (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-44142258 (BBC)]

;Disasters and accidents
*Five people are confirmed dead as thunderstorms hit the [[Northeastern United States]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/US/dead-severe-thunderstorms-batter-northeast-400k-power/story?id=55170362 (ABC News)]
*The [[Luxembourg]] [[The Greens (Luxembourg)|Green Party]] politician and government secretary [[Camille Gira]] dies after he collapsed while delivering a speech to [[Chamber of Deputies (Luxembourg)|parliament]]. [http://delano.lu/d/detail/news/gira-tributes-asselborn-summons-tusk-criticism/179250 (Delano)]

;International relations
*[[2017–18 North Korea crisis]]
**[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
***[[North Korea]] cancels high-level talks with South Korea in protest of [[United States Forces Korea|United States–South Korea joint military]] exercises. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-15/north-korea-suspends-talks-with-south-over-u-s-military-drills (Bloomberg)]
**[[2018 North Korea–United States summit]]
***North Korea warns that it might cancel talks with the United States if the U.S. keeps insisting that North Korea will "unilaterally" abandon [[North Korea and weapons of mass destruction|its nuclear weapons program]], similar to the [[disarmament of Libya]]. The White House says it is hopeful the planned summit will still happen. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/north-korea-threatens-to-cancel-summit-with-trump-over-military-drills/2018/05/15/04a15a5e-5878-11e8-8b92-45fdd7aaef3c_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-missiles-usa/white-house-u-s-still-hopeful-for-north-korea-summit-idUSKCN1IH1O3 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[USA Gymnastics sex abuse scandal]]
**[[Michigan State University]] announces that it will settle with sexual assault victims of [[Larry Nassar]] for over $500 million. [http://wkar.org/post/report-msu-pay-least-500-million-nassar-surivivors-settlement#stream/0 (AP via WKAR)]
*Five people are shot dead and another is injured in a shooting at a house in [[Ponder, Texas|Ponder]], [[Denton County, Texas]]. The [[Denton County Sheriff's Office (Texas)|Denton County Sheriff's Office]] believe the shooter is among the dead. [https://www.nbcdfw.com/news/local/Police-Investigate-Incident-at-Denton-County-Home-482804161.html (NBC)]
*A mass grave containing the bodies of 12 people is discovered in [[The Gambia]]. The victims were allegedly killed in 2005 by paramilitary forces controlled by former president [[Yahya Jammeh]], according to human rights groups. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2018/may/16/mass-grave-victims-alleged-massacre-gambia (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Media of Kenya]]
**Kenyan President [[Uhuru Kenyatta]] signs a law outlawing cyber-espionage, cyber-bullying, and the "publication of [[false information]]." [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-kenya-lawmaking/kenyas-president-signs-cybercrimes-law-opposed-by-media-rights-groups-idUSKCN1IH1KX (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Politics of Malaysia]]
**Malaysian longtime opposition figure and leader of incumbent government party [[Pakatan Harapan]], [[Anwar Ibrahim]] is released from prison after obtaining a full royal pardon from King [[Muhammad V of Kelantan|Muhammad V]]. Anwar was imprisoned in 2015 during the tenure of [[Najib Razak]] for charges widely considered to be politically motivated. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-malaysia-politics-anwar/malaysias-anwar-walks-free-after-royal-pardon-meets-mahathir-idUSKCN1IH09T (Reuters)] [http://www.malaysiandigest.com/features/737884-anwar-ibrahim-returns-today.html (''MalaysianDigest'')] 
*[[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**A Belgian judge withdraws the [[European Arrest Warrant]] against [[Toni Comín]], [[Lluís Puig]] and [[Meritxell Serret]] amid procedural defects and irregularities. The [[Supreme Court of Spain]] criticizes the decision as a "lack of commitment to Spain" from the Belgian justice. [http://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20180516/443616717683/fiscalia-belga-rechaza-entrega-exconsellers-toni-comin-meritxell-serret-lluis-puig-pablo-llarena-espana.html (''La Vanguardia'')] [http://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20180516/443620694472/tribunal-supremo-ausencia-compromiso-euroorden-belgica-comin.html (''La Vanguardia''<sub>2</sub>)]<!--see talk-->
*[[Trump campaign–Russian meetings]]
**The [[United States Senate Committee on the Judiciary|U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee]] releases 2,500 pages of documents related to a June 9, 2016 meeting between [[Donald Trump 2016 presidential campaign|Donald Trump campaign]] officials and Russian attorney [[Natalia Veselnitskaya]]. [https://www.npr.org/2018/05/16/611477917/senate-committee-releases-2-500-pages-about-2016-trump-tower-meeting (NPR)]
